reason: The 18-atom set is C7H9NO, consistent with a disubstituted aromatic/aryl system with a hydroxyl O and an amino N. Conformational freedom is dominated by rotation about the aryl-C bonds linking the OH and NH2 substituents. In this class intramolecular O···N proximity is the dominant stability discriminator: a folded geometry that brings the hydroxyl donor close to the amino acceptor allows an intramolecular O-H···N hydrogen bond and better dipole alignment, whereas extended geometries keep O and N far apart and pay an entropic/strain penalty with no compensating H-bond. O···N distance was therefore used as a practical proxy for H-bond accessibility and overall compactness. Distances were estimated from the given Cartesian coordinates for each conformer. The smallest O···N separations are ~4.5-4.9 Å for 13, 28 and 9, which is the range where an O-H···N contact can be made in a disubstituted aryl system, suggesting a favorable folded H-bonded form. 21 is the next most compact at ~5.6 Å. The mid-range cluster 3,22,1,2,26,15,30,16,4,18,10,11,6 is ~6.0-7.0 Å, i.e. essentially non-H-bonded but not highly strained. The most extended forms 8,27,20,5,23,6 etc. show O···N >7.3 Å and 12 and 24 are the most extended at >8.1 Å, implying no intramolecular contact and maximal chain/aryl rotation strain. Atoms 1–6 form the carbon backbone, atom 3 is the ether/ester O linked to C2 and atoms 8–9 are the terminal peroxide. With no experimental energies the order can only be inferred from geometry. The dominant contributions for an acyclic / macrocyclic peroxide are gauche/anti populations along C1–C2–O3–C4–C5–C6 and non-bonded H…H/O…H contacts. As a first-order proxy the end-to-end separation between the terminal carbon C1 (atom 1) and the peroxide oxygen O8 (atom 8) correlates with chain extension: larger C1…O8 distances correspond to more anti, extended backbone geometries with fewer eclipsed/torsional strains and less close H…H overlap, whereas very short C1…O8 distances correspond to folded geometries with increased gauche interactions and higher steric crowding around the O–O moiety. Distances were estimated from the given coordinates, e.g. ~4.88 Å for conformer 15, ~4.93 Å for 10, ~4.97 Å for 26/8, up to ~6.19 Å for 14 and ~6.13 Å for 6. The longest separations therefore represent the least strained extended conformers and are placed at the top of the stability estimate, the shortest separations represent the most folded/crowded conformers and are placed at the bottom. intramolecular O…H contacts that could provide weak H-bond stabilisation to the peroxide oxygens are not quantified here and would tend to favour intermediate compactness; this is an acknowledged source of uncertainty and the ranking is a geometry-based estimate with essentially isoenergetic groups expected within ~0.1–0.2 Å of each other. The permutation below follows the descending C1…O8 end-to-end metric, i.e. most extended / least gauche strain first.
